- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is above recent lows, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent price history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down), suppress forecast overshoots in the next 3–5 days.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, reduce the spike magnitude by 10–20% to avoid overreacting to sentiment reversal.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, apply a 5–10% downward bias to the forecast mean to reflect potential continuation.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low) and forecast is inconsistent with recent trend, align forecast to the most recent 5-day moving average.
